{{Short description|Japanese clan}}
{{Infobox Japanese clan|founder=[[Kamuyaimimi]]|parent house=[[Imperial House of Japan]]|cadet branches=[[Aso clan]]}}
{{Nihongo|'''Ō clan'''|多氏|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}} is a descendant clan of [[Jimmu]] and [[Himetataraisuzu-hime]]. They are descended from [[Kamuyaimimi]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Grapard |first=Allan G. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NxS7EAAAQBAJ&dq=%22%C5%8C+clan%22&pg=PA35 |title=The Protocol of the Gods: A Study of the Kasuga Cult in Japanese History |date=2023-04-28 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-91036-2 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1QPXAAAAMAAJ&q=%22%C5%8C+clan%22 |title=Tenri Journal of Religion |date=1968 |publisher=Tenri University Press |language=en}}</ref>

[[Ō no Yasumaro]] was a famous member. He became head of the clan in 716 around the time he wrote the [[Kojiki]].<ref name="ReferenceA">''Obunsha Japanese Encyclopedia 3rd Edition''</ref><ref>Aston (1995:xv)</ref>

== Relationship with Takemikazuchi ==
{{Main|Takemikazuchi}}
[[Takemikazuchi]] was originally a local god ([[kunitsukami]]) revered by the Ō clan,<ref name="gakken">{{cite book |last=小向 |first=正司 |title=神道の本 |publisher=学研 |year=1992 |series=Books Esoterica |volume=2 |pages=76–7}}(zasshi code 66951-07; kyōtsu zasshi code T10-66951-07-1000)</ref> and was a god of maritime travel.<ref name="gakken" /> However, the [[Nakatomi clan]] who also has roots in this region, and when they took over control of priestly duties from the Ō clan, they also instituted Takemikazuchi as the Nakatomi clan's [[ujigami]] (clan deity). Or so this is the observation by {{Interlanguage link|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup}} in his ''Jinja to kodai ōken saishi'' (1989). He goes on to theorize that the Ō clan was originally {{Nihongo|ōmi|大忌|"greater taboo (priesthood)"}}, but was usurped by the Nakatomi who were among the "lesser priesthood" (the latter claims descent from the {{Nihongo|[[Inbe clan]]|[[:ja:忌部氏|忌部氏]]}}).<ref name="gakken" />
